About SafeRide Health

Getting to the doctor should never be the reason someone goes without care. SafeRide Health exists to remove that barrier. We are a technology and services company rebuilding non-emergency medical transportation, pairing our own technology with a national network of vetted transportation providers so that payers and health systems can get members to dialysis, chemotherapy, behavioral health, and primary care reliably and affordably.
It is a rare combination of things to work on: measurable, real-world impact on people who need it, wrapped inside a genuinely hard technology and logistics business. Every single trip involves a member, a clinical need, a provider, a network, a payer contract, and a cost curve. Getting all six right at the same time, at national scale, is the problem we get to work on.
We serve the largest Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, and provider programs in the country. We are a Series C company at approximately $750M in annual run rate with 300+ employees, growing quickly and, unusually for this stage, meaningfully profitable. That last part matters more than it sounds: it means we can build for the long term rather than sprint toward the next raise, and it means the decisions you help make here have real money attached to them.
The industry is moving too. Benefit designs keep shifting, payers are under genuine cost pressure, and the tooling for running a national transportation network (routing, forecasting, automation, AI in the contact center) is far better than it was two years ago. Very little about how this business should be run is settled yet. That is the fun part.
The team you would join
Strategy & Operations is SafeRide's internal consulting team. We are who the company calls when a problem is ambiguous, cuts across several functions, or needs an answer that nobody currently owns.

The work sits where healthcare, logistics, and technology meet, which is not a combination you find in many jobs, and it comes with unusual access: this team sees the whole P&L and works directly with the leaders who own it.
One thing makes us different from an external consulting firm. Our clients are internal, so we do not hand over a deck and leave. We stay until the change is live, adopted, and visible in the number. A brilliant analysis nobody adopts is a failed project here, which means the job is as much about judgment, communication, and persistence as it is about analytical horsepower.
Increasingly, that work sits between Operations, Product, and Data Engineering. SafeRide is in an exciting growth phase, streamlining how the business runs and leaning into newer, faster technology, including AI, agentic tools, and better data infrastructure, and S&O is where operating needs get turned into clear product and data requirements. The people who thrive here are technically fluent operators: comfortable in the data, able to translate a messy operating problem into something Product and Engineering can build, and credible on both sides of that table.

We are fully remote and have been from the start, with the team distributed across the US. What we ask in return is clarity: say what you are working on, say what you found, and say what you think should happen next.

About the Team

Klaviyo's Strategic Finance & Analytics team helps leaders understand, measure, and plan for business performance. We work closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Go-to-Market, and Finance partners to turn complex data into financial insight that informs investment decisions, planning, and long-term growth.

As Klaviyo expands its platform and launches new AI-powered products, more of our business is becoming consumption-based. That makes it increasingly important to connect what customers do on our platform to what we earn and what it costs us to deliver.

About the Role

We're looking for a Lead Strategic Finance & Analytics Engineer to build and maintain the models that forecast Klaviyo's recognized revenue and cost of goods sold (COGS). This role blends data science, finance, and data engineering. You'll build scalable, production-quality forecasting systems, and you'll understand the financial mechanics well enough to make them useful for planning.

The role starts with a focus on recognized revenue forecasting. From there, you'll build out COGS forecasts, beginning with consumption-aligned infrastructure costs such as message sending and LLM usage, and extending to the rest of our cost base. As more of our products move to consumption models, the systems you build will be the foundation for how we plan, price, and understand margin.

You'll report into Strategic Finance & Analytics and partner closely with FP&A, Product, Engineering, Data Science, and Go-to-Market teams. This is a hands-on technical role. You'll own models end to end, set standards for how forecasts are built and evaluated, and help the team grow its capabilities.

How You'll Make a Difference

• Build and maintain forecasting models for recognized revenue and COGS. Start with overall recognized revenue, then extend to consumption-aligned infrastructure costs (message sending and LLM usage first) and, over time, the full COGS base, including cloud infrastructure, SMS and email carrier and vendor costs, AI inference, and support.

• Connect product workloads to unit economics. Work with Engineering, Product, and Finance to link usage drivers (such as message volume, profile growth, channel mix, and AI feature usage) to both revenue and delivery costs.

• Build forecasts that scale with the business across multiple time horizons and levels of granularity, designed to extend to new consumption-based products as they launch.

• Partner with Finance and FP&A to understand planning mechanics and modeling assumptions, and translate them into robust, well-documented frameworks that feed budgeting, rolling forecasts, and long-range planning.

• Monitor model performance over time , tracking accuracy and bias, detecting drift, and building challenger models to keep forecasts resilient.

• Lead variance investigations when actuals diverge from forecast, separating data issues, model limitations, customer behavior, pricing or product changes, and external factors.

• Run scenario and sensitivity analyses to evaluate pricing changes, product launches, vendor and infrastructure decisions, and cost-efficiency initiatives.

• Partner with Analytics Engineering on reliable pipelines and dbt models that give forecasting a clean, trusted foundation.

• Establish technical standards for forecasting methodology, evaluation, and code quality.

• Communicate clearly to technical and non-technical audiences ,

Product Manager

Digitalzone is a B2B marketing company building the demand orchestration systems that connect buying signals to revenue. Our products turn scattered signals into pipeline our customers can act on. As we continue to grow, we are looking for a Product Manager to join the product team and help shape where these products go next.

POSITION OVERVIEW
As a Product Manager, you own the strategy and delivery of our demand orchestration products. Your deep understanding of B2B marketing and lead generation, combined with strong product management craft, will be central to aligning product strategy with business objectives. You will work closely with engineering, data science, design, and marketing; make decisions grounded in data; and keep a clear line of sight from customer problems to revenue outcomes.
We also expect a modern toolkit. Product managers here use AI tools in their daily work to move faster: to synthesize research, to build a rough prototype that makes an idea concrete, and to tighten the loop between an idea and real user feedback. Those tools support the fundamentals, they do not replace them. Judgment is still the job.

Key Responsibilities

•
Product strategy: Own the roadmap for demand orchestration and align it with company objectives, connecting product decisions to outcomes such as SQLs, high intent leads, and marketing sourced and influenced revenue.

•
Customer and market understanding: Conduct market research, track competitors and industry trends, and maintain a deep working knowledge of lead generation and B2B marketing processes.

•
Discovery and user research: Talk to customers regularly, run interviews and usability sessions, and turn what you learn into prioritized product decisions.

•
Requirements and definition: Write clear PRDs, user stories, and acceptance criteria. Where a prototype communicates the intent better than a document, build one.

•
Prioritization: Make explicit trade-offs about scope, sequence, and what will not get built, and explain the reasoning to stakeholders.

•
Cross-functional collaboration: Partner with engineering, data science, design, sales, and marketing to take products from concept through launch and adoption.

•
Agile delivery: Run disciplined iterative development: short cycles, working software each sprint, and steady progress against the roadmap.

•
Data-driven decision making: Define success metrics before launch, instrument what you ship, and read the results honestly afterward.

•
Go-to-market partnership: Support launches with positioning input, enablement material, and a clear view of the customer value being delivered.

•
Communication: Articulate product vision and requirements to audiences ranging from engineers to executives to customers.

•
Problem solving: Break down ambiguous problems, including the newer ones that come with building AI powered features.

Ways of Working We Value
The fundamentals above are the core of the role. These practices are how we expect a PM to apply them today.

•
Prototyping: Comfort turning an idea into something tangible within days, whether that is a wireframe, a clickable Figma flow, or a rough working prototype. A prototype in front of a user answers questions a specification cannot.

•
User experience design: Strong instincts for information architecture, user flows, and interaction design. You can give a designer specific, useful feedback rather than adjectives.

•
Practical AI fluency: You use AI tools in your own work: synthesizing research and feedback, drafting and pressure testing documents, exploring data, and generating edge cases. You know where these tools help and where they add risk or noise.

•
Building with AI tools (vibe coding): Willingness to use AI assisted coding tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, Lovable, Replit, or v0 to stand up a prototype yourself. You do not need to be an engineer. You do need to be curious enough to try.

Qui sommes-nous ?
Télécom Paris, école de l’IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) et membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris, est une grande école du top 6 des écoles d’ingénieurs généralistes françaises.
La Raison d’Être de Télécom Paris est de former, imaginer et entreprendre pour concevoir des modèles, des technologies et des solutions numériques au service d’une société et d’une économie respectueuses de l’humain et de son environnement.

Nous recherchons notre futur(e) post-doctorant(e) en IA agentique correcte par construction (SoS) pour rejoindre le département INFRES de Télécom Paris.

Contexte scientifique :

les cadres de vérification existants supposent généralement des modèles finis et précisément définis, dont les actions et les relations de transition sont connues. Ces hypothèses sont difficiles à maintenir dans les systèmes modernes d’IA agentique, où les actions peuvent être générées dynamiquement, les environnements peuvent évoluer et les informations sur le système peuvent être incomplètes.
Le projet Sound or Silent (SoS) vise à combler cette lacune en étudiant une nouvelle approche d’IA agentique correcte par construction. L’idée centrale consiste à intégrer le raisonnement stratégique et la vérification formelle directement au processus décisionnel des agents autonomes. Au lieu de vérifier un agent uniquement après son développement ou de surveiller son comportement après l’exécution, SoS étudie la possibilité de produire des actions formellement certifiées conformes à une spécification donnée. Selon cette approche, une action candidate n’est exécutée que s’il est établi qu’elle appartient à une stratégie garantissant les propriétés requises. Si une telle garantie ne peut être établie, l’agent s’abstient d’agir.
Atteindre cet objectif exige d’étendre les techniques de vérification stratégique à des environnements ouverts, évolutifs et partiellement spécifiés, et d’étudier des notions de correction adaptées à une information incomplète. Le projet explorera également une architecture associant un composant génératif non fiable, chargé de proposer des actions ou des stratégies candidates, à un noyau de vérification formelle de confiance, chargé d’en contrôler la correction. Une attention particulière sera portée à l’expressivité des modèles formels sous-jacents, au coût de calcul de la certification et au compromis entre garanties formelles et capacité des agents à accomplir des tâches utiles.
Les travaux associeront des développements théoriques à la réalisation et à l’évaluation expérimentale de prototypes, dans des scénarios de planification autonome, d’agents d’IA utilisant des outils et de coordination multi-agents. L’objectif général est de poser les fondements de systèmes d’IA agentique dont l’autonomie est encadrée par des garanties stratégiques formellement vérifiables.

Vos missions principales seront de :

• Mener des travaux de recherche sur l’IA agentique correcte par construction

• Assurer des missions d’encadrement et de tutorat

• Contribuer au rayonnement scientifique de Télécom Paris

Vous devrez être titulaire d’un doctorat ou d’un diplôme équivalent et disposer de solides connaissances en méthodes formelles, logique et vérification de modèles. Une expérience dans les systèmes multi-agents, les logiques stratégiques, la vérification à l’exécution ainsi que dans le développement d’agents fondés sur les grands modèles de langage (LLM) sera également attendue.

Vous devrez maîtriser le développement logiciel et l’implémentation d’algorithmes, ainsi que la démarche de recherche scientifique, notamment la formulation de problématiques, la conception d’expériences et l’analyse de leurs résultats. Une excellente maîtrise de l’anglais, à l’écrit comme à l’oral, sera indispensable.

Enfin, vous devrez faire preuve d’un bon esprit d’équipe, de qualités relationnelles et pédagogiques, de bonnes capacités rédactionnelles ainsi que d’un esprit de synthèse.

You will build Blueberry's customer success function, not inherit someone else's. Every customer we've won becomes yours to grow, and the way we onboard, retain, and expand accounts will be the way you designed it.

You'll work directly with our Founder & CEO and CTO, sit in the room with marketing leaders at some of the biggest consumer brands in the world, and see your feedback ship in the product within days.

Exceptional performance creates a path to leading Blueberry's entire post-sales organization.

Every time Anthropic releases a model, we publish a system card: a long-form technical document that describes the model's capabilities, safety properties, evaluation results, and the reasoning behind our deployment decisions. System cards are some of the most consequential and widely read documents we produce, and they are one way we hold ourselves publicly accountable for the safety claims we make.
